title: Bus purchases, school zone speeds and winter road authority
subtitle: Also: lawsuit settlement, art gallery grants, Provincial Offences Court judges, respiratory season update and Fischer-Hallman Road closure.
overview: Regional Council approved the purchase of eight hybrid and electric transit buses from Nova Bus Inc. and named it vendor of record for future orders. Council also extended the busPLUS feeder service contract with Voyageur Transportation Services for two years from April 2024.

On roads, Council lowered posted speed limits in regional school zones, with Snyder's Road in Wilmot kept as it is today and staff asked to report on a flashing light system there. It also let the Commissioner of Transportation Services declare a Significant Weather Event and pass that authority on to the three cities. This affects winter road maintenance. A portion of Fischer-Hallman Road was closed and part of Eagle Street North was added to the regional road system.

Council approved a settlement of a lawsuit with Kieswetter Excavating, restored operating grant eligibility for public art galleries from January 2024, and agreed to ask the province for more Provincial Offences Court judicial resources. The Medical Officer of Health reported elevated COVID-19 activity and a rise in invasive Group A Strep. A councillor withdrew a notice of motion after provincial clarification.

decisions.detail: Council accepted Nova Bus Inc.'s proposal to supply eight buses for $9,595,992.00 plus taxes and named it vendor of record through 2025, with options to renew to 2028.
Council extended the Voyageur Transportation Services contract for two years from April 1, 2024 at an estimated $2,605,000.00 plus taxes.

decisions.item: School zone speeds and weather event authority
decisions.detail: Council permanently lowered school zone speed limits (keeping Snyder's Road, Wilmot as is and asking staff to report on flashing lights), delegated Significant Weather Event declarations to the Commissioner of Transportation Services, closed part of Fischer-Hallman Road, added part of Eagle Street North to the regional road system and approved a Corporate Asset Management Policy {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved a $700,000 settlement of Kieswetter Excavating Inc. v. the Region, covering all compensation, holdbacks, interest and costs {{vote:m7}}.
Council reinstated public art galleries as eligible for operating support through Council-approved grant programs effective January 1, 2024 {{vote:m10}}.

decisions.item: Provincial Offences Court resources and corporate vision
decisions.detail: Council will ask the Ministry of the Attorney General for adequate judicial resources for the Region's Provincial Offences Court and approved refreshed vision, mission and core value statements {{vote:m9}}.

debate: Little debate took place on the finance reports, closed committee settlement or committee summaries. The chair saw no questions or speakers and each item went to a vote.
One councillor with a pecuniary interest in a gallery client declared a conflict, so the art gallery grant item was taken separately from the other Administration and Finance items.

The Medical Officer of Health told Council that COVID-19 remains elevated but fluctuating, with RSV and influenza low, and that invasive Group A Strep is rising across the province. She urged residents to keep vaccinations current. One councillor thanked public health for a mobile vaccination bus visit to Wilmot.

The Medical Officer of Health said public health clinics will shift to children under five from December 1. Enforcement of school immunization records resumes next year, with suspension notices starting in February for elementary and April for secondary students.
A councillor explained the withdrawn notice of motion: the provincial housing minister had made clear who should respond, which in essence covered the motion.
